questions.question: What is required to establish COPD in the appropriate clinical context under current guidance?
choices: Post-bronchodilator spirometry showing persistent airflow obstruction
A smoking history alone
Chronic cough alone
A chest radiograph alone
questions.explanation: Symptoms and exposures raise suspicion, but spirometry demonstrating persistent post-bronchodilator airflow obstruction is used to confirm COPD in the appropriate clinical setting.

questions.question: Why can two patients with similar spirometry have very different dyspnea burden?
choices: Dynamic hyperinflation, deconditioning, cardiac disease, anxiety, nutrition, and comorbidities also affect symptoms
Spirometry has no value at all
Dyspnea is always caused only by anxiety
Symptoms are unrelated to COPD
questions.explanation: COPD symptoms reflect respiratory mechanics plus comorbid cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, psychological, and social factors. Function and trajectory must be assessed.

questions.question: Before escalating COPD inhaler therapy, what should be assessed?
choices: Diagnosis, device technique, adherence, access, exposures, comorbidities, and alternative causes of dyspnea
Only the number of inhalers listed
Whether the patient can name a brand
Nothing if the patient has a COPD diagnosis
questions.explanation: A patient may seem uncontrolled because of misdiagnosis, incorrect technique, cost barriers, smoke exposure, heart failure, infection, or other causes rather than an insufficient regimen alone.

questions.question: Which intervention is especially disease-modifying for a patient with COPD who smokes?
choices: Repeated, supported smoking-cessation treatment
Avoiding all physical activity
Using oxygen solely because of dyspnea
Waiting for a hospitalization before discussing tobacco
questions.explanation: Smoking cessation is one of the most important interventions for COPD progression and overall health. It requires repeated support, not blame after recurrence.

questions.question: A patient with a COPD label develops orthopnea, leg edema, and rapid weight gain. What is the best FNP reasoning?
choices: Assess for heart failure and other causes; do not assume all dyspnea is COPD
Treat only with a rescue inhaler
Ignore the edema
Wait for the next spirometry appointment
questions.explanation: Heart failure can mimic or coexist with COPD. New volume-related symptoms require cardiopulmonary assessment and safe disposition.

questions.question: What is the purpose of observing a patient use an inhaler?
choices: To identify technique, coordination, device mismatch, and education needs that can cause apparent treatment failure
To decide whether the patient deserves treatment
It is unnecessary if a prescription was filled
To diagnose pneumonia
questions.explanation: Device demonstration is a clinical examination. Correct technique and a device the patient can use and afford may be more important than a nominal dose increase.

questions.question: Which finding during a presumed COPD exacerbation most strongly supports emergency evaluation?
choices: New oxygen requirement with confusion and severe work of breathing
Stable chronic sputum without change
A normal refill request
Mild symptoms improving with the patient’s plan
questions.explanation: New oxygen need, altered mental status, cyanosis, exhaustion, hypotension, severe distress, or concern for pneumonia, PE, ACS, sepsis, or heart failure requires urgent assessment.

questions.question: Why should oxygen not be prescribed solely because a patient reports dyspnea?
choices: Oxygen need requires appropriate assessment of oxygenation and clinical context
Dyspnea is never serious
All COPD patients already have oxygen
Oxygen replaces smoking cessation and inhalers
questions.explanation: Dyspnea has many causes. Oxygen therapy is based on clinical assessment and requires safety education, monitoring, and consideration of the underlying problem.

questions.question: Which is a key feature of post-exacerbation COPD care?
choices: Prompt review of trigger, technique, medication reconciliation, access, oxygen needs, prevention, and follow-up
No follow-up after emergency treatment
Assume the discharge list matches home medicines
Avoid pulmonary rehabilitation discussion
questions.explanation: Post-exacerbation follow-up is a high-value safety visit. It prevents repeat events by addressing causes, device use, access, comorbidities, and transition gaps.

questions.question: When should pulmonary referral be considered?
choices: Diagnostic uncertainty, frequent exacerbations, advanced symptoms, difficult inhaler strategy, or concern for another lung diagnosis
Only after no longer using tobacco
Never for recurrent hospitalizations
Only for one resolved viral cough
questions.explanation: Pulmonary consultation can clarify diagnosis, phenotype, spirometry, treatment strategy, oxygen or ventilatory assessment, and advanced symptom management.
